findings.title: ROADMAP.md (plan of record) is a month behind actual steering and its sequencing points at the wrong engine
findings.claim: The P0-P8 plan of record records nothing after 2026-08-09 (§2.5) and still sequences aeon-first, while every phase actually executed since (UX overhaul stages 1-4 plans 1-6, art authoring 1/2A/2B/2C) was classic-first and off-roadmap.
findings.evidence: git log master --since=2026-08-15 -- docs/ROADMAP.md is empty while master gained ~190 commits since 2026-08-14. Row-by-row against code: P0 doc hygiene NOT done (ART_SUITE.md still says s4_engine and documents the deleted Toolbar UI); P1 export retirement NOT done (src/core/export/vram-coloring.ts, act-descriptor.ts, entity-data.ts all still present); P2 NOT started (src/main/aether/ contains adapter.ts+protocol.ts only — server side; no outbound client, the suite keystone per empyrean/docs/ROADMAP.md ~line 200 'crown jewel'); P3 open; P4-P6 still engine-gated and unmoved; P7 row says Import pipeline 'None' (ROADMAP.md:161) while src/core/art/png-import.ts + the import path shipped 2026-08-16 (commits 1ba9dd5, f942119, eb370ee); '~83 test files' (ROADMAP.md:57) vs measured 205 files / ~2250 tests (2026-08-14-plan6-handoff.md baseline; 171 *.test.ts in src today). Off-roadmap deliveries not recorded anywhere in it: DocumentHistoryHub undo unification, facet parity/LevelWorkspace unification (LegacyWorkspace/ClassicProjectView/ZoneActTree/Toolbar deleted — confirmed absent from src), art convergence H1-H3, art-authoring phases 1-2C.
findings.fix: DECISIONS, not options. (a) Add §2.6 recording the August line (UX stages 1-4, art authoring 1-2C) as delivered, same style as §2.5. (b) Re-sequence around the classic spine the owner is actually steering: NEXT PHASE = classic collision authoring — colind/heightmap assignment plus solidity in the classic art facet, reusing aeon's CollisionPalette idiom (this is exactly 'bring aeon's approach into classic'). Why it is the single highest-leverage phase: 2C's own out-of-scope note (phase-2c spec §8) concedes 'authoring collision for brand-new chunks still has no in-app answer' — a committed drawing gets colind 0 + solidity 0 (classic-commit-plan.ts:412-413) and the player falls through it; classicSetColind is reachable only from agent-handler.ts. Every rung of originate→constrain→import→commit→refine now exists in-app; collision is the one rung that still sends the artist out of Aurora, which is the precise failure the 'artists don't leave' bar forbids, at the last step. (c) SECOND = the playtest loop, classic-first (build.lua invoke + emulator launch), then the aeon Aether outbound client per P2 — the suite keystone stays on the board but behind the loop the current product actually needs. (d) Mark P7's classic half DONE, P8 substrate DONE (already noted), and demote P4-P6 to an explicit 'awaiting aeon engine tasks' parking section so cold sessions stop treating them as next.

verdict.reasoning: Every factual link verified independently at 2b38e0b. (1) Currency: docs/ROADMAP.md's newest commit is f007245 (2026-08-09); `git log --since=2026-08-14` on master returns 190 commits, none touching the file, while the doc's own header (line 7) mandates in-place updates and line 13 claims "Last full revision: 2026-07-03". (2) Row-by-row: src/core/export/ still holds vram-coloring.ts, act-descriptor.ts, entity-data.ts (P1 retirement §4.2 not done); src/main/aether/ contains exactly adapter.ts + protocol.ts, no client.ts (P2 §4.8 not started); ROADMAP.md:161 says Import pipeline "None" although src/core/art/png-import.ts and the end-to-end import path shipped 2026-08-15/16 (1ba9dd5, eb370ee); line 57's "~83 test files" measures 171 (`find src -name '*.test.ts'`); P0 doc hygiene is unapplied — docs/ART_SUITE.md:12 still says s4_engine and :73 tells the user to click the Art button "in the Toolbar" while no Toolbar/LegacyWorkspace/ClassicProjectView/ZoneActTree file exists under src. (3) The August line (UX stages 1-4, art authoring 1/2A/2B/2C) exists only under docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-08-1* and is recorded nowhere in ROADMAP.md, whose §5 table stops at the §2.5 row and still sequences P4-P6 behind aeon engine tasks. (4) The fix's cited premise also holds: classic-commit-plan.ts:411-413 gives a cell with no displaced predecessor `solidity = 0` and `colind = 0` (inheritance applies only where `old` exists — correctly scoped by the seat to brand-new chunks); classicSetColind's only non-test caller is agent-handler.ts:713, corroborated by src/core/project/s1/index.ts:76-80 ("Classic has no collision-editing UI… sole collision affordance is a read-only overlay") and by the 2C spec's own out-of-scope note at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-phase-2c-resolve-and-commit-design.md:495. I searched for a superseding plan-of-record that would make the staleness harmless and found none — no newer roadmap exists, and the 2026-08-12 UX and 2026-08-15 art-authoring specs still reference ROADMAP.md. No link in the chain breaks.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> medium. Nothing here is executable: docs/ROADMAP.md produces no wrong runtime output, breaks no main-path feature, and destroys no user work — the panel's "high" bar is not met. The harm is real but indirect and fully reversible by editing one file: a cold session reading the self-declared plan of record is told a shipped feature is "None" (line 161), that the suite has ~83 test files when it has 171 (line 57), that "P0-P3 are unblocked today" (line 344), and is pointed at aeon-gated P4-P6 as next. That is directive-grade misinformation about project state, which warrants medium, not the wrong-output/broken-feature tier.

findings.title: 2C spec header says BUILT, but D2b's cross-act reach reporting is not built
findings.claim: The spec's D2/D2b requirements — palette-adoption dialog names the actual files from paletteSources (SBZ per-act palettes), report names SBZ3-borrows-LZ-art and ending-reuses-GHZ reach, LZ/SBZ3 underwater-palette warning — are all unimplemented, yet the status header declares the phase BUILT with no deviation note.
findings.evidence: grep for SBZ/borrow/sibling/ending/underwater/paletteSources across src/core/art/classic-commit-plan.ts, src/renderer/components/canvas/canvas-commit-model.ts and CommitPlanView.tsx returns nothing. The only adoption warning is the generic hardcoded sentence at classic-commit-plan.ts:263 ('every act composed from the same palette file is affected') — the exact class of sentence D2 said must be computed from the profile, not hardcoded. The spec §7 test 'the water-palette warning fires for LZ' does not exist (grep water/SBZ in __tests__/classic-commit-plan.test.ts: no hits). The planner takes no profile input at all (CommitPlanInput, classic-commit-plan.ts:49-71), so it structurally cannot compute reach. Failure scenario: an artist commits while editing LZ, adopts a palette, and is never told SBZ3 renders the same art under a palette they never saw — the 'wrong output the artist was not warned about' D2b exists to prevent.

verdict.reasoning: Independently verified at SHA 2b38e0b. Spec line 3 declares "Status: BUILT 2026-08-16" with no deviation note, and §8's out-of-scope list does not include D2b or D2's file-naming requirement. Implementation: classic-commit-plan.ts contains exactly two warnings.push sites — line 263 ('the zone palette changed: every act composed from the same palette file is affected') and line 444 (GHZ $51/$28 loop alias) — both hardcoded strings. CommitPlanInput (lines 49-71) has no profile, act ref, or paletteSources field, so the planner structurally cannot compute reach; planFromSnapshot (canvas-commit-model.ts:~200) passes nothing extra; CommitPlanView.tsx holds `ref` (line 35) but uses it only for the "into GHZ 1" label (103) and the applied toast (92), and its adopt-chip tooltip (149) repeats the same hardcoded sentence. Repo-wide grep for paletteSources|underwater|borrow hits only profiles/s1.ts, s1-io.ts:341, s1-levelart-reservations.ts:43 and test fixtures — nothing on the commit path. The §7 test "the water-palette warning fires for LZ" does not exist: classic-commit-plan.test.ts:148 asserts only toMatch(/every act/), and water|SBZ|reach have no hits in that file. The reach itself is real (profiles/s1.ts:481-496: SBZ act 3 takes LZ_TILES, map16/LZ.eni, map256/LZ.kos, collide/LZ.bin while keeping basePalette('SBZ Act 3.bin') plus its own underwater files), so an artist committing chunks while editing LZ does change SBZ3 and is never told. Refutation attempts failed: no deferral/carry-forward note in plans/2026-08-15-2c-foundations.md or 2c-resolver.md, and no separate reach-reporting module anywhere in src. Triggering state: any commit with paletteResolution='adopt-into-zone', or any chunk-replacing commit in LZ/GHZ — the report's warnings array carries at most the generic palette sentence and the $51 alias.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> medium. The finding is anchored to a documentation line and the harm is a missing advisory, not wrong output. Nothing is corrupted or lost: the adoption write goes through doc.palettes -> s1-io decomposition into the act's own paletteSources, so SBZ's per-act palette files are correctly isolated, and the whole commit is one undoable ART_DOMAINS record. The seat also overstates the shipped sentence — "every act composed from the same palette file is affected" is hardcoded but remains TRUE in SBZ (whose acts use different palette files); D2's objection was to the false form "every act of the zone changes". So the artist sees an under-informative true statement, not a misleading one. Main-path commit works and was CDP-verified. That is spec-vs-code drift plus an unbuilt advisory requirement — medium, not "wrong output or broken main-path feature".

findings.title: The whole art-authoring line shipped with zero MCP parity, against the standing cross-cutting rule
findings.claim: Paint-through, canvas documents, canvas commit and PNG import (phases 1-2C) have no MCP tools, violating ROADMAP.md:332-334's rule that every new authoring capability ships its MCP tools in the same phase so agent and human editing stay equivalent.
findings.evidence: grep commit_canvas/import_art/canvas across agent-handler.ts and docs/MCP.md: no authoring tool hits (only map-canvas screenshot plumbing). classicPaintSurface, classicCommitCanvas and the PNG import path are human-gesture-only. This is a direction breach, not just debt: the suite's agent-equivalence principle is one of Aurora's two structural rules, and 2C's planner is pure and refusal-typed — i.e. it was built to be agent-callable and then wasn't exposed.
findings.fix: Decide it as scope, not backlog: the collision-authoring phase (A1's next phase) ships paint_collision AND retrofits commit_canvas + import_art_sheet in the same phase, restoring the invariant in one pass.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to break the claim on the facts and could not. Verified independently:

(1) The rule exists as cited. docs/ROADMAP.md, section "Cross-cutting (all phases)": "MCP parity rule: every new authoring capability ships with its MCP tools in the same phase (the ~17 new tools across #6–#9), one undo step per mutation, so agent and human editing stay equivalent."

(2) src/main/editor-methods.ts is the SINGLE source of MCP tools — src/main/mcp-server.ts:33 registers exclusively via `for (const m of EDITOR_METHODS)`, there is no second registration site. Its complete 34-entry name list (lines 48–155) has no commit_canvas, no import_art_sheet, no canvas/paint-surface tool. So there is no back door the seat missed.

(3) src/renderer/agent/agent-handler.ts: all 33 `case` labels enumerated; none are canvas/commit/import. The only `canvas` occurrences are the map-canvas screenshot plumbing at lines 545–562 — exactly as the seat characterised it.

(4) docs/MCP.md read in full (169 lines): no canvas, commit, or import tool documented.

(5) The line did ship at this SHA: commits f942119 (png-import), c16f61c (commit panel), b95052b (classicCommitCanvas), 1ba9dd5 (PNG sheet import end to end), e9850ca (marks 2C built); the design doc docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-in-app-art-authoring-design.md carries the banner "phases 1, 2A and 2B built and merged (2026-08-15)".

So the factual core — art-authoring phases 1–2C have zero MCP tools while ROADMAP declares a same-phase parity rule — is true.

Two corrections to the seat's framing, both material:

(a) It is NOT a fresh direction breach. The classic surface has never had any pixel-level agent tool: `write_tiles` is aeon-only (agent-handler.ts:250-252 calls requireProject() then reads ctx.zone.tileset.tiles), and classic pixel editing (TileTab) was human-only before phase 1 ever existed. The gap also runs the other way — the 2C spec itself, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-phase-2c-resolve-and-commit-design.md:495, records "classicSetColind exists but is reachable only from agent-handler.ts", i.e. an agent-only capability with no human editor. The invariant was already unheld on the classic surface in both directions; phases 1–2C continued that state rather than breaking a standing one.

(b) The proposed fix is partly already-done and partly name-colliding. `paint_collision` already exists (editor-methods.ts:70, agent-handler.ts:324) as the aeon section-plane painter, and a classic collision tool cannot reuse that name — editor-methods.ts:145-148 documents that this registry is flat and MCP tool names must be globally unique (the reason classic's palette tool is named set_level_palette rather than set_palette).

Bash stopped returning output partway through the session (echo itself began failing), so I could not run the test suite or grep for the classicPaintSurface/classicCommitCanvas symbol bodies. That link is unverified only as to exact symbol spelling — commit b95052b's subject line names classicCommitCanvas directly, and it is immaterial to the verdict, which rests on the tool registry being demonstrably empty of these capabilities.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> low. The panel rubric reserves "high" for wrong output or a broken main-path feature. Nothing here produces wrong output and nothing is broken: the human authoring path was CDP-verified end to end (commit e9850ca), and no agent call returns bad data because no such agent call exists. There is no triggering input or state to state — the finding describes an ABSENCE of an agent-facing surface on a surface (classic) that already lacked pixel-level agent tools entirely, and which conversely already carried an agent-only tool with no human UI (set_colind). This is roadmap-adherence / scope-planning debt, correctly raised, but it is not a defect. The seat's own words give it away: "This is a direction breach, not just debt" is an editorial framing, not a failure path.

findings.title: 2C's shipped tests skip three named spec §7 disciplines
findings.claim: Spec §7 requires reclaim guards planted against real s1disasm GHZ data, an id-space off-by-one plant (engine id vs file index freeing a neighbour's art), and pipeline step 9's zeroing of stale reclaimed block ids with a report count; none of the three exists.
findings.evidence: grep s1disasm/GHZ in classic-commit-plan.test.ts and canvas-resolve.test.ts: zero hits — all 48 planner tests are synthetic fixtures, the exact 'fixtures tidier than reality' class the spec §7 names as the session's dominant defect. grep 'engine id|file index|off-by-one': no id-space plant test. In the planner, leftover reclaimBlocks past reclaimBlockCursor (classic-commit-plan.ts:342-343, 386) are neither zeroed nor reported, so a replace that reclaims more blocks than it re-mints leaves stale BlockDefs pointing at reallocated tiles — spec step 9 calls this out ('garbage in BlockTab, so zero them and say how many'). The id-space risk is real: UsageIndex.blockToChunks is FILE order while chunkPlacements is ENGINE id, and only convention separates them.
findings.fix: Add the three items before the next phase builds on the planner: real-GHZ reclaim plants, the engine-id-vs-file-index plant, and stale-block zeroing + report field.

findings.title: The art spec's three §7 open decisions are already decided by shipped code — ratify them so they stop being re-litigated
findings.claim: All three 'open' decisions were settled de facto during the build; the spec still lists them open, inviting a cold session to redesign shipped behaviour.
findings.evidence: Decision 1 (tool-mode vs separate surface): shipped as an explicit per-tier Assign|Paint mode inside ChunkTab/BlockTab — ChunkTab.tsx:34 ('paint is an explicit per-tier mode, not an armed tool'); the Assign-black regression through this seam was already found and fixed (2b38e0b). Decision 2 (naming): shipped as 'Canvas' in the explorer (eb370ee) persisting to <project>/.aurora/canvas/<name>.png + <name>.canvas.json (canvas-file.ts:6,44) — deliberately Aseprite-openable per §4.1. Decision 3 (free-slots vs whole-pool): shipped as BOTH — budgetReadout prints 'tiles N unique · M free in <ACT> · pool used/total' (use-canvas-constraints.ts:106-120) and deliberately does not compare them, with 2C's commit report supplying the computed comparison (phase-2c spec §6).
findings.fix: RATIFY all three as-built and mark §7 resolved: (1) tool-mode per tier, no separate surface — one place per tier held up under the round-trip bug and its fix; (2) 'Canvas' in UI, .aurora/canvas/<name>.png + <name>.canvas.json on disk — the open-format goal is met, do not invent a proprietary extension; (3) show both numbers with the comparison living only in the commit report — honest and expected at once, and it is what 2C already computes.
